articles.title: Nightmare
articles.summary: Near-black satin body with three soft glowing amber-orange blobs floating on it. Reads as an almost-black purple car with a few dim orange blobs; from a distance the speckle disappears and the glows fade to warm smudges.
articles.what: Up close: Very dark aubergine-black surface with a fine grain of dim violet and red pixel speckle. Three soft, blurry amber-orange glows about 70-100 px across float on it, like distant streetlights through fog or eyes in the dark. No lines or shapes, only the glows. From a distance: Reads as an almost-black purple car with a few dim orange blobs; from a distance the speckle disappears and the glows fade to warm smudges. Measured spec (average): metal 19, roughness 91, coat 55. Shine: satin. Metal: none. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hood, hero panel.
Fits: show car, stock car, gt / sports car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Nightmare on the hood".
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: wide panels let the glows spread out
Quarters: glows form soft accents
White, yellow or orange numbers read well on the dark; dark numbers vanish.
Stripes, camo or graphics in lighter colours: the near-black ground shows them off
Pairs well with: orange, copper, black, deep red.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a bright neon: glows are dim orange smudges
Not smooth black: it has fine speckle and soft blobs
Avoid: glow spots can clash with number placement, very dark in sim shadows.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 19 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 91 (satin gloss), clearcoat 55 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: glow spots can clash with number placement, very dark in sim shadows.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: stripes, camo or graphics in lighter colours: the near-black ground shows them off; fine mesh or carbon at low strength: adds texture without losing the stealth
Patterns to avoid: bright glitter patterns: ruin the moody dark; busy geometric patterns: bury the glows
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: deepens the black; fine flake at low strength: adds a starry sheen
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark areas swallow the veins in the sim, numbers need light outline.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: stripes or lettering in white: readable on the dark ground; fine mesh at low strength: texture without more clutter
Patterns to avoid: other yellow or squiggle patterns: pile up; bold camo: muddy the filaments
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: lifts the yellow and deepens the black; fine flake: low strength only, matte look is part of it
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

examples.title: Ask for it by name
examples.goal: See Ns2 Dendrite Choir on the car.

settings.AI copilot (✦ AI button): put Ns2 Dendrite Choir on the hood
